root_cause: The login route is intentionally noindex and should stay outside sitemap/indexable SEO inventory, but the technical SEO link validator assumed every internal destination must itself be an indexable canonical route. Simply excluding inloggen.html therefore made every global login link fail. The missing concept was an explicit public utility-route class: valid internal destination, intentionally non-indexable.
prevention: Model public utility routes explicitly: valid internal destinations that remain outside sitemap/indexable SEO inventory.
Authentication/login utility pages that are noindex must not be forced into the sitemap merely to satisfy internal-link validation.
Technical SEO must allow links to explicitly classified utility routes while continuing to fail on unknown or accidental non-indexable destinations.
Keep utility-route classification in the shared route contract so sitemap generation and technical SEO consume the same authority.
Guard both exclusion from indexable scope and acceptance as a utility link target with executable regressions.

evidence.diagnose_failure: 430 internal links to /inloggen were rejected after the route was removed from indexable SEO scope
